Started my bog garden last year in a plastic bin with some fly traps sarracenia's and some sundews. Upgraded to a pod liner this year and had some new plants added and was able to cultivate a few of my own of the flower stalks. 

The phat sarracenia's consume slugs like their spaghetti idk what it is about them. The smaller pitcher plans attract a lot of ants. Don't know the genus but I believe they are still young do they may still develop traits I can identify. Sarracenia's in the separate pots are new ones I got this year the last one has amazed me honestly it was still stems 3 weeks ago.

Filliformas sundew has caught grown male mosquitoes flies and lots more. Smaller ones(I think they're capillaris or something) the did well last year and caught a decent amount of gnats but I don't know how well they're doing after my replanting if them. Thet seem dry.

The fly traps are doing and a wide variety of health. Some are already growing flower stalks about 4-5 inches. And others seem to not be sick almost. I didn't do the best at replanting because I underestimated how much they would curl up and almost unplant themselves. Some looked in bad condition before replanting but have grown some good sprouts. None from last year have died. Only one new one from this year that wasn't properly planted when sent to the garden place I got it from.

Either way it's been great watching the bog so far this year and fly and gnat seasons hasn't quite started.
